title: Marine Biologist Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Understand the marine biologist salary landscape in Australia. Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual pay using 38-hour weeks, plus tax and super guidance from Fair Work and A
salarySummary: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour ($33.05 casual), but marine biologist salaries vary by award; use the ABS full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week as a benchmark for professional roles.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a marine biologist in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single award rate for marine biologists published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (or $33.05 for casuals) is the legal floor. Most marine biologists are covered by the Professional Employees Award or similar, which sets higher minimum rates. Use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator to find the correct award rate for your role.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a full-time role based on 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay. For example, $40 per hour gives $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040 per year. Remember to add superannuation (12% on top) and deduct tax using the 2026–27 resident rates.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the advertised salary?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your base salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. When comparing job offers, check whether the advertised figure is base salary or total package (including super). Our calculator shows super as an additional amount.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Marine Biologist Salary Landscape

If you're researching a **marine biologist salary** in Australia, you'll find that pay varies widely depending on experience, employer, and location. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that median weekly earnings for marine biologists are not publicly available at the six‑digit occupation level, but the broader category of life scientists provides a useful benchmark. According to the ABS Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours (May 2025), full‑time adult ordinary time earnings across all occupations average $2,083.70 per week. This figure, from the on‑site reference tables, is a helpful starting point for professional roles.

However, the legal minimum you must be paid is set by the National Minimum Wage or an applicable award. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that an employee aged 21 or over must receive at least $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 per hour if they are a casual employee not entitled to paid leave. These rates apply from 1 July 2026. For marine biologists, the relevant award is likely the *Professional Employees Award* or a similar industry award, which typically sets higher minimum rates than the national minimum. Always check your specific award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the safety net. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, equating to $1,004.90 per week. For casual employees, a 25% loading is added, making the minimum $33.05 per hour. However, most marine biologists will be covered by an award that prescribes higher rates, penalty rates for weekends or overtime, and allowances. The Fair Work Commission's annual wage review sets these award rates each year. If you are award‑free, the national minimum applies.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. The annual pay is calculated using the standard formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full‑time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

- Hourly rate $30 → $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year
- Hourly rate $45 → $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920 per year
- Hourly rate $60 → $60 × 38 × 52 = $124,800 per year

If you are casual, tick the casual loading checkbox and the tool adds 25% to your base rate before calculating. For example, a base rate of $30 becomes $37.50 per hour with loading, giving $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100 per year.

You can also work out your fortnightly pay by multiplying the weekly amount by two. For a $30 per hour full‑time employee, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly pay is $2,280 before tax and super.

### The Role of Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading as compensation for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). This loading is paid on top of the base hourly rate. When using our calculator, **never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it automatically when you check the box. The Fair Work Ombudsman confirms that the casual loading for award/agreement‑free employees is 25%.

### Superannuation and Tax Considerations

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross pay is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your salary; it's an extra cost to the employer.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low income earners). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide explains how to estimate your net income after tax and Medicare.

### Using the Calculator for a Marine Biologist Salary

Because the ABS does not publish median weekly earnings specifically for marine biologists, you can use the average weekly earnings for all full‑time adults ($2,083.70) as a rough guide. That equates to an hourly rate of about $54.83 (based on 38 hours). However, actual salaries depend on your award classification, experience, and employer (e.g., government, university, or private sector). The Jobs and Skills Australia profile notes that marine biologists commonly work in Professional, Scientific and Technical Services, Public Administration and Safety, and Education and Training.

To get a personalised estimate, enter your actual or expected hourly rate into [the timesheet](/). The tool will show your annual gross pay, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember that the result is an estimate – it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice.

### Key Takeaways

- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour ($33.05 casual) from 1 July 2026.
- Marine biologists are likely covered by an award with higher minimums – check with the Fair Work Ombudsman.
- Annual pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Assume 38 hours for full‑time.
- Super is 12% on top of your gross pay, up to the contribution cap.
- Use our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) for more details on award rates and tax brackets.

Always verify your specific pay conditions with your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman. The figures here are a guide, not a determination of your exact pay.
